original_metadata.name: Old St Paul’s Cathedral, London
original_metadata.era: Hollar later pre-1666 state: classical west portico and square central tower WITHOUT the medieval tall spire. Exact snapshot year not claimed.
original_metadata.reason: Coherent Hollar series supplies all four exterior orientations and scaled ground plan, adequate for major masses/roof silhouette/large openings in a preparation sheet.
geometry: Long cruciform church: nave, projecting transepts, choir, massive square crossing tower.
Do not add the lost medieval spire: all selected elevation prints consistently show the later truncated tower.
West: classical colonnaded portico below gabled nave, paired small turret peaks. East: tall Gothic gable with very large rose/tracery opening.
North and south elevations differ in annexes and treatment; trace them independently.
Steep longitudinal roofs over nave/choir, transverse roofs at transepts, lower aisle roofs; Gothic choir has pinnacled buttresses.
S1 establishes footprint and side chapter-house/cloister relation. Upper surfaces invisible in prints may be simplified explicitly, not labeled surveyed.
gaps: Ready means reference eligibility for proportion-based major-volume preparation, not a metric-accurate reconstruction or owner acceptance.
Exact print date is unspecified in Commons metadata; preserve Hollar attribution and depicted-phase interpretation.
All views are one artist/collection series, not independent surveys. Graphic scale has not been cross-checked with a second dimensional source.

qa.historical_phase: Recognisably old Palais du Trocadero, with rotunda and twin towers rather than the later Chaillot palace.
qa.main_shape: Central rotunda, twin towers and end pavilions are recognisable, but lateral galleries are compressed so severely that the overall footprint/mass balance is wrong.

issues.region: Both wings and central-body-to-overall-width ratio
issues.finding: T3 full-width photograph shows very long low galleries extending far beyond the compact central body; generated wings are much shorter relative to the rotunda/twin-tower group. Central body occupies a substantially larger share of the whole palace. This is a principal footprint/mass error, not microornament uncertainty.

issues.region: Rotunda upper facade and tower/roof profile
issues.finding: Generated rotunda drum becomes a regular set of tall glazed arches and simplified conical roof; T1/T3/T4 show more articulated bays and roof transitions. Tower caps and pavilion roofs are also simplified. These reinforce caution but the decisive FAIL is the shortened wings.
